title: code-review-pr-scratchpad-evelyn-park
content:
PR: #3428 — kv-cache + batching refactor (draft)
Author: @morgan-li
Branch: feature/kv-cache-refactor
Related ticket: ENG-781

Context / goal:
- Unify per-request KV cache behavior across streaming and non-streaming paths.
- Move batching logic out of request_handler.py into batch_scheduler.py to support dynamic batch window configs.
- Fix a race where a streaming connection could drop KV entries on early cancel.

Quick summary of changes (files):
- runtime/kv_cache.py: rework API (get_prefix, materialize_prefix) and replace global CacheEntry with CacheSession.
- runtime/batching/batch_scheduler.py: new module, centralizes batch queue + policy.
- runtime/request_handler.py: reduced, delegates to batch_scheduler.
- tests/test_kv_cache.py, tests/test_batching_integration.py: new/updated tests.
- examples/streaming_demo.py: updated to use CacheSession.

High-level concerns / risk areas:
- Concurrency: CacheSession lifecycle is now tied to request IDs; need to ensure sessions are cleaned on timeout/cancel. Potential memory leak if cancel path doesn't call close().
- Compatibility: Public API changed (some internal call sites still call old methods). There are adapters in place but not on all code paths (see comment in request_handler.py line ~120).
- Performance: Batch scheduler introduces an extra event loop hop per request — benchmark impact unknown. Need microbenching for p99 latency with small seq-len (8–32).
- Streaming regressions: streaming_demo updated, but I didn't see tests for partial response + cancel scenario beyond a unit test. Add integration test with simulated client cancel.

Checklist (quick) — run locally before merging:
- [ ] Run unit tests: pytest -q tests/test_kv_cache.py
- [ ] Run integration: pytest tests/test_batching_integration.py -k streaming -q
- [ ] Run perf harness: tools/perf/run_epoch.py --profile p99 --workload=small_seq
- [ ] Manual smoke: start local runtime, run examples/streaming_demo.py and cancel midway, observe no KV growth in /tmp/kv_metrics.log

Inline comments / suggested changes (by file):
- runtime/kv_cache.py
  - L32-L40: the new CacheSession API is cleaner but relies on weakrefs to track active sessions. Weakrefs + asyncio tasks can be subtle — prefer explicit close() in cancel path and a finalizer as fallback.
  - get_prefix() docstring should state whether it returns a copy or a view; implies callers mutate returned dict (tests assume immutable). Make explicit.
  - materialize_prefix: currently does IO (s3 get) inline on first miss. This blocks the batch scheduler thread; recommend converting to async materialize() and await in batch path.

- runtime/batching/batch_scheduler.py
  - line 78: the batching policy default window is 5ms — that's aggressive for small instances. Consider adaptive windowing based on observed inter-arrival; see notes in optimize/quantization for similar heuristic.
  - how are heterogeneous sequence lengths handled? The current code forms batches by arrival time only; need a path to split by max_tokens to avoid OOM on long seqs. Add bucket_by_seq_len option.

- runtime/request_handler.py
  - line ~120: adapter for old_cache.get() present but not used in streaming path — add explicit call in StreamRequestHandler.
  - error handling: on exception in streaming yield loop, CacheSession.close() is not called. Wrap yield in try/finally.

Testing notes / gaps:
- Missing: end-to-end test that exercises streaming client cancel + subsequent request reusing same token prefix (ensures KV entries not lost/corrupted).
- Add stress test that sends high-concurrency small requests to batch scheduler to validate batching policy and measure latency distributions.
- Flaky tests observed locally: tests/test_batching_integration.py::test_stream_cancel sometimes times out (timeout 5s). Increase timeout or make deterministic by mocking time.sleep in scheduler.

Follow-ups / TODOs (post-merge or before):
- [ ] Add explicit CacheSession.close() calls in all cancel/timeout paths (critical).
- [ ] Add async materialize_prefix to avoid blocking scheduler.
- [ ] Add bucket_by_seq_len heuristic and a config knob exposed in runtime config (default off).
- [ ] Add integration test for streaming cancel (see above).
- [ ] Run perf job on staging (bench/kv-batching-2026-02-28) compare p50/p99 vs main.
- [ ] Update docs in docs/runtime/kv-cache.md to reflect new API and migration notes for internal consumers.

Notes to author (tone: constructive):
- Nice cleanup overall — CacheSession boundary makes ownership clearer.
- A couple of places where synchronous IO sneaks back in; that's the main risk for perf regressions.
- Please add a short migration note in PR description listing known call-sites that still use old API and the adapters implemented.

Random implementation ideas / refactor thoughts (braindump):
- Consider making CacheSession a context manager and using contextvars to propagate current session instead of passing session explicitly through many call sites. This reduces plumbing noise.
- For batching, explore using an adaptive leaky-bucket that expands window slightly when observed batch sizes < target. We already have telemetry for arrival times; could bootstrap without new instrumentation.
- For materialize_prefix, if first lookups are common hot paths, introduce a small in-memory LRU for recently-materialized prefixes to avoid repeated s3 calls during rollout. Use the same eviction policy as the main KV cache.

Small nit TODOs / editorial:
- Update inline TODOs in code to include ticket id (ENG-781) to avoid losing follow-ups.
- Add metric: kv_session_count{state="active"} and kv_session_lifetime_seconds histogram.

Local debug commands I ran:
- pytest tests/test_kv_cache.py -k session -q
- python -m examples.streaming_demo --host localhost --port 8080 (cancel with ctrl-c at ~1s)
- tail -f /tmp/kv_metrics.log | grep Session

Questions for author / reviewers:
- Was the sync s3 get in materialize_prefix deliberate for simplification? If yes, what perf tradeoffs were measured?
- Is there an expected upper bound on active sessions per worker? If not, we should cap and emit telemetry to detect leaks.

Final recommendation (preliminary):
- Blocker: ensure CacheSession.close() is called reliably on cancel/timeout.
- Non-blocking but strong ask: convert materialize_prefix to async.
- Otherwise, good to iterate in a follow-up after adding the two tests and running perf comparisons.

---
Notes to self (Evelyn):
- Follow up with @morgan-li for clarification around materialize_prefix (add comment in PR).
- If PR lands with adapter path, schedule a small canary on staging and run perf harness.
- Add ENG-781 follow-up ticket for metrics + session leak detection.

end of scratchpad.
